cell.label: Adult with recent vision loss. Transient (<24 h) monocular vision loss?
Suspect temporal arteritis (eg, older than 50 years, jaw claudication, head pain, fever)?
Eye pain present, especially with eye movement?
Acute onset of light flashes and/or floaters?
Hypertensive or history of vascular disease?
Patient diabetic with evidence of diabetic retinopathy on examination?
Consider open angle glaucoma or age-related macular degeneration. Refer to general ophthalmologist for evaluation.
Optimize diabetes management; refer to retinal specialist for full retinal assessment and initial treatment.
Consider retinal artery/vein occlusion or ischemic nonarteritic optic neuritis. Refer urgently to retinal specialist.
Suspect retinal detachment; refer to retinal specialist as an emergency.
Suspect acute optic neuritis. Urgent neuro-ophthalmologist referral for further revaluation (eg, MRI, lumbar puncture, tests for syphilis and tuberculosis, CXR, and antinuclear antibodies).
CRP, ESR, CBC, and emergent referral for temporal artery biopsy. Initiate steroids prior to biopsy results.
Consider cerebrovascular disease, cardiac embolic disease, or intracranial mass. Order appropriate imaging urgently.

algorithm.title: Monocular Vision Loss in Individuals Younger Than 18 Years: Diagnosis.

cell.label: Monocular vision loss or suspected loss.
History of trauma or evidence of child abuse?
Associated with progressive eye turn or leukocoria?
Rule out retinoblastoma.
Associated with frank papilledema?
Rule out uncorrected or undercorrected refractive error.
Suspect brain tumor, meningioma and/or congenital CNS malformation. Order MRI and obtain neuro-opthalmologic consult.
Slowly progressive cataract, iridodialysis.
Associated with eye pain?
Associated with a perilimbal injection; pain not associated with eye movement.
Suspect anterior or retrobulbar optic neuritis.
Obtain MRI of brain and optic nerves. Rule out demyelinization. Obtain neuro-ophthalmologic consult.
Suspect anterior uveitis or corneal injury.
Obtain eye consult.
History of eye trauma or evidence of child abuse?
Suspect intraocular injury/retinal detachment, dislocated lens, hyphema.
Evidence of leukocoria or eye turn?
Evidence of unilateral large eye with enlarged corneal diameter and/or tearing?
Suspect congenital glaucoma.

algorithm.title: Binocular Vision Loss in Individuals Younger Than 18 Years: Diagnosis.

cell.label: Binocular vision loss.
Associated with hearing loss, poor night vision, color vision deficiency, or family history of inherited retinal disease?
History of headache and evidence of papilledema?
Suspect uncorrected or undercorrected refractive error or malingering.
Suspect brain tumor and/or congenital CNS malformation, hydrocephalus or pseudo tumor cerebri. Obtain brain imaging and ophthalmologic consult.
Suspect hereditary retinal disease.
History of trauma, head injury or evidence of child abuse?
Suspect cortical injury, bilateral vitreal hemorrhage, or bilateral retinal injury. Obtain brain imaging, ophthalmologic consult, and possibly child protective services.
Evidence of hypoxic ischemia in the perinatal period, or meningitis/encephalitis?
Evidence of present or recent flu-like illness?
Rule out disseminated encephalomyelitis secondary to infectious or inflammatory disease process. Obtain infectious disease and ophthalmologic consult.
Bilateral disc edema present?
Associated with bilateral perilimbal injection and eye pain not related to eye movement?
Perform physical examination with CBC and comprehensive metabolic panel; rule out diabetes mellitus; obtain eye consult.
Probable anterior uveitis. Rule out probable autoimmune disease based on signs and symptoms; obtain eye consult.
Suspect bilateral optic neuritis.
Obtain brain imaging and ophthalmologic consult.
Suspect cortical vision impairment.
